title: Child and Adolescent Development from a Cultural Perspective
description: Theories of child and adolescent development using a cultural and contextual approach with emphasis on self-reflection and lifelong learning. Liberal studies premajors and majors and students seeking teaching credentials will complete Teacher Education 170; all others will complete
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Field Experience in Mathematics
description: Guided classroom observations for prospective middle and high school mathematics teachers. Mathematics education and strategies that promote professional development. Teaching in culturally and linguistically diverse school settings.

title: Field Experience in Science
description: Guided classroom observations for prospective middle and high school science teachers. Science education and strategies that promote professional development. Teaching in culturally and linguistically diverse school settings.

title: Field Experience in Social Science
description: Guided classroom observations for prospective middle and high school social science teachers. Social science education and strategies that promote professional development. Teaching in culturally and linguistically diverse school settings.
notes: Recommended for students interested in pursuing a career in social science teaching. To include 15 hours of classroom lecture/discussion and 15 hours of activity in the field.

title: Health Education for Teachers
description: Topics designated in health framework for California; infusing health topics in the K-12 general curriculum. For multiple or single subject candidates.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: The Teaching Profession: First Clinical Experience
description: Concepts and theories for the teaching profession; guided student observation and participation in public school classrooms.

title: Universal Design For Learning
description: Introduction to methods and theories of digital teaching and learning through demonstration, simulation, facilitation and performances that integrate the tools of technological knowledge with content and pedagogical knowledge. Hyflex mode of delivery. Support for service-learning tutoring.
notes: The service-learning credit requires 2 hours per week in partnerships with local school sites. Placement in service-learning sites requires a minimum of 2.5 GPA. For more information, direction on placement, TB test and livescan, please contact the SDSU Pathways office at Pathways@sdsu.edu. Enrollment in this section entails participation in experiential learning and/or internshnip. These experiences may occur on-campus or off-campus. Additional requirements may apply. Course contains a service-learning opportunity; contact instructor for details.

title: Fieldwork in Community Settings
description: Tutoring process and teaching strategies for the content being tutored.

title: Foundations of Education
description: Combines disciplines of anthropology, economics, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology to introduce student to concepts and generalizations informing the teaching and learning process in modern classrooms.

title: Writing in Educational Settings
description: Composition of texts for K-12 educational situations and audiences. Critical reading and writing skills to support K-12 students learning.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Science Fieldwork in Community Settings
description: Science teaching and learning to include supervised fieldwork in local science classrooms.

title: Ethnic Identity Development in Education
description: Ethnic and racial identity exploration and development through curriculum for improving academic achievement of students in K-12 schools. Ethnic and racial socialization of children and identity exploration of American ethnic groups.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Assessment in Mathematics Education
description: Techniques to assess and develop students’ mathematical understanding. For use by elementary and secondary classroom teachers and mathematics education specialists.

title: Children’s/Adolescents’ Literature
description: Survey of children’s/adolescents’ literature and its incorporation into the classroom curriculum.

title: Comics for K-12 Educators
description: Examination and analysis of comic texts for K-12 classroom purposes; to include history of censorship and socio-political significance of comic texts; emphasizes development of K-12 students’ literacy and critical thinking skills.

title: Topics in Teacher Education
description: Designed to meet the needs of individuals or groups of teachers who wish to develop or continue the study of some problem.
notes: See

title: Curriculum Development in Education
description: Advanced study of the research in curriculum development, construction and evaluation.

title: Innovations in Instruction
description: Exploration of innovative instructional practice in the public and private schools, with emphasis on innovative teaching strategies. An evaluation of the motivational effect and structural validity of promising instructional practices.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content; only six units may be applied toward a master’s degree.

title: Seminar in Science in Elementary Education
description: Advanced study of the problems of teaching science in the elementary school with emphasis on the literature of science education.

title: Teaching Critical Thinking Using Technology
description: Critical thinking and educational technology. Educating diverse learners.

title: Teaching Online: K-12 Curriculum and Instruction
description: Skills and knowledge for the development and implementation of K-12 curriculum using evidence and research supported pedagogy toward producing high-quality online instruction. To include related research, history, philosophy, controversy, and innovative technologies.

title: Technology Equity in K-12 Learning Communities
description: An examination of pedagogies and practices of equity and access in 21st Century K-12 learning communities.

title: Seminar in Literacy and Language Arts
description: Trends in reading instruction to include developmental sequences in reading skills and abilities, reading in the content fields, individual differences and interests.

title: Seminar in Language Arts
description: Advanced study of problems in teaching language arts. The study of the scientific research and application in the field.

title: Leadership in Literacy Education
description: Planning, presenting, and evaluating professional development activities in literacy education for teachers at the K-12 level.

title: Assessment of Reading and Language Arts
description: Theoretical knowledge and practical skill in assessing reading and language arts using both formal and informal measures.

title: Instructional Strategies for Reading and Language Arts
description: Supervised teaching experience utilizing instructional activities in individual and small group settings.

title: Topics in Reading Education
description: A variety of instructional sequences (mini-courses), each focusing on a single topic or competency dealing with reading instruction.
notes: See

title: Literacy and Language
description: Theories of literacy and methods for developing literacy in language, reading and writing. Instructional methods and assessment techniques for children and adults.

title: Planning for Teaching and Assessment in Writing
description: Comprehensive writing instruction in context of the interactive language arts. Development of plans for curriculum and instruction in diverse classrooms. Examination of multiple assessments and how they inform instruction in K-12 classrooms.

title: History of Social Studies Reform
description: History and current status of social studies curricula in American schools, K-12. Emphasis on issues, controversies, competing philosophies, historical trends, and applications.

title: Sociocultural Foundations of American Education
description: Historical and philosophical nature of American schools as it relates to equity, pedagogy, and curriculum. Issues of equity, race, culture, gender, ethnicity, sexual preference, and social issues as they impact the classroom.

title: Research-Based Pedagogy for Diverse Learners
description: Research-based pedagogy for diverse learners. Instructional strategies applicable across disciplines.

title: Advanced Secondary Science Teaching Methods
description: Advanced instructional methods for teaching secondary science to foster scientific thinking and practices with a focus on research-based principles of effective and inclusive instruction.

title: Advanced Secondary Mathematics Teaching Methods
description: Advanced instructional methods for teaching secondary mathematics to foster conceptual understanding and problem-solving with a focus on research-based principles of effective and inclusive instruction.

title: Measuring and Assessing Student Achievement in Schools
description: Development of assessments and tests common in instructional and research contexts. Uses and interpretation of assessment data in given differential social/political contexts. Implications for research and instruction.

title: Selected Topics in Teacher Education
description: Intensive study in specific areas of teacher education.
notes: See

title: Inclusive Education
description: Research, theory, and practice of inclusive education to include examination of the politics of disability in the public schools and American society.

title: Action Research in Learning Environments
description: Capstone course for Master of Arts in Teaching degree. Action research conducted in students’ own teaching environments.

title: Seminar in Teacher Education
description: Intensive consideration of selected topics of current importance in teacher education.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. 6 units applicable to a master’s degree. For collaborative induction programs with school districts: up to 12 units applicable to a master’s degree.

title: Special Study
description: May involve fieldwork.

title: Classroom Environment
description: Develop a classroom plan encompassing different aspects of teaching and learning that work together in promoting and maintaining a positive climate for learning and for the social-emotional development of all students.
notes: Reserved for students admitted to the Single Subject Teaching Credential program and SS - Integrated Teacher Education Program.

title: Learning Environment
description: Skills in interpreting the legal aspects of education, identifying various kinds of school and classroom organization, and using instructional media and verbal stimuli to facilitate learning.

title: Secondary School Student Teaching Seminar
description: To plan and organize instruction in relation to all competencies acquired and to be implemented in an on-site, full-time student teaching assignment.
notes: See

title: Teaching Mathematics in Preschool through Elementary School
description: Instructional methods for development of children’s conceptual understanding, computational, and problem-solving skills in mathematics, including use and development of materials and programs.

title: Teaching Social Studies in the Elementary School
description: Developing curriculum, principles and materials of instruction, including instructional media and participation in elementary social studies education.

title: Teaching Science in Preschool through Elementary School
description: Developing research-based science curriculum, principles and materials of instruction, including instructional media and participation in preschool through elementary science education.

title: Instructional Methods for Mathematics
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in mathematics. To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for History and Social Sciences
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in history and social sciences. To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for Science
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in sciences. To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for English Language Arts
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in English Language Arts (ELA). To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for Physical Education
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in physical education. To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for Music
description: Teaching strategies and assessment in music. To be taken concurrently with student teaching.

title: Instructional Methods for Teaching Theatre
description: Explores drama and theatre in educational settings to facilitate engaging experiences for theatre learners. Teacher candidates participate in lesson design for theatre and drama and reflect on instruction, pedagogy, and theories of drama in theatre arts.

title: Interdisciplinary Single-Subject Methods
description: Teaching concerns, instructional planning and materials, classroom management, measurement and evaluation, effective discipline, curriculum, computer literacy, special problems encountered in teaching, career planning, and school-community communication processes.

title: Instructional Methods for Visual Arts
description: Explores visual arts in educational settings to facilitate engaging experiences for art learners. Teacher Candidates participate in lesson design for art and reflect on instruction, pedagogy, and theories in visual and media arts.

title: Behavioral and Psychological Aspects of Teaching
description: Teacher competencies as they relate to learning theories, adolescent growth, self-assessment, measurement and evaluation.
notes: See

title: Psychological Foundations of Education
description: Implementing learning process through interactive skills, using instructional principles to facilitate learning and changes in behavior and techniques used in assessing instruction and pupil growth.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching Mathematics
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary mathematics instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching History/Social Science
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary history/social science instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching Science
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary science instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching English Language Arts
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary English language arts instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching Physical Education
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary physical education instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching Music
description: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary music instruction.

title: Advanced Methods in Teaching Theatre
description: Instructional Methods for Theatre explores drama and theatre in educational settings to facilitate engaging experiences for theatre learners. Teacher Candidates participate in lesson design for theatre and drama and reflect on instruction, pedagogy, and theories of drama in theatre arts.
notes: Best practices, evaluation of student work, learning assessments, and pedagogy in secondary theatre instruction.

title: Advanced Instructional Methods for Visual Arts
description: Explores advanced topics in the teaching and learning of visual and media arts in K-12 educational settings. Teacher Candidates participate in lesson and unit design for art and reflect on instruction, pedagogy, and theories in art.

title: Advanced Instructional Methods in Dance
description: Explores dance in educational settings to facilitate engaging experiences for dance learners. Teacher Candidates participate in lesson design for dance and reflect on instruction, pedagogy, and theories in dance.

title: Teaching Reading and Language Arts in Preschool through Early Elementary
description: Selecting, designing, and evaluating appropriate learning experiences to assure children’s growth in reading and language arts. Includes nature of reading and language arts as a human behavior, various approaches, materials, and techniques used in teaching reading and language arts.
notes: Cannot be taken for credit if 6 units of TE 930 have been earned.

title: Teaching Reading and Language Arts in Upper Elementary School
description: Selecting, designing, and evaluating appropriate learning experiences to assure children’s growth in reading and language arts in upper elementary grades. Includes various approaches, materials, and techniques used in teaching reading and language arts.
notes: Cannot be taken for credit if 6 units of TE 930 has been earned

title: Teaching of Literacies in the Secondary School
description: Teacher competencies and skills to include reading/writing and diagnosing literacy needs in content areas. For students completing a credential at SDSU, this course must be taken concurrently with enrollment in first or second semester single subject credential program.

title: Humanistic and Social Aspects of Teaching
description: Teacher competencies as they relate to values, awareness, self-concept, rights and responsibilities.
notes: See

title: Basic Student Teaching Seminar
description: Discussion of immediate problems in student teaching with emphasis on children’s growth and development.

title: Advanced Student Teaching Seminar
description: Discussion of immediate problems in student teaching with emphasis on the influence of philosophical, social and cultural factors on learning.

title: Secondary School Student Teaching I
description: On-site, part-time experience to implement teacher competencies developed in

title: Secondary School Student Teaching (Advanced)
description: On-site, full-day experience to implement teacher competencies as developed from the total professional sequence. Student must provide own transportation to student teaching site.
notes: *Imperial Valley Campus credential candidates should enroll in the 15 unit course section.  Other candidates consult your advisor or follow directions provided by your program.

title: Basic Student Teaching in Preschool through Elementary School
description: Day-to-day teaching experiences including selected instructional activities for which a teacher in a classroom is normally responsible.

title: Advanced Student Teaching in Preschool through Elementary School
description: Teaching experiences including all the instructional activities for which a teacher in a classroom is normally responsible.
notes: *Imperial Valley Campus credential candidates should enroll in the 15 unit course section.  Other candidates consult your advisor or follow directions provided by your program.

title: Elementary School Student Teaching
description: On-site, full-day teaching experiences. Two consecutive eight week assignments at two different broad levels of schooling. Each eight week assignment will provide typical responsibilities of teachers through a graduated series of experiences, such as class preparation, instruction of students, maintaining accurate student records, attending faculty meetings and parent conferences.

title: Secondary School Student Teaching
description: On-site, full-day teaching experiences. Two consecutive eight week assignments in single subject content area; one in junior high school and one in senior high school. Each eight week assignment will provide typical responsibilities of teachers through a graduated series of experiences, such as class preparation, instruction of students, maintaining accurate student records, attending faculty meetings and parent conferences.
